title: Far-right AfD wins state election in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, CDU fails to enter parliament
summary: The far-right AfD has come first in the state election in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, with Chancellor Merz's CDU failing to enter parliament. Meanwhile the Left Party took first place in Berlin.…
byline: Darko Janjevic, Richard Connor, Kieran Burke, Roshni Majumdar

image.caption: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the two state election outcomes 'a disaster'Image: Christian Mang/REUTERS

blocks.text: AfD wins election in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania — election commission

The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won the state election in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, while the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) failed to secure any parliamentary seats.

According to the preliminary results announced by the election commission early Monday morning, the AfD secured 38.2% of the vote on Sunday. The Social Democratic Party (SPD), which is led by state premier Manuela Schwesig, garnered 35.5% of the vote.
The socialist Left Party (6.5%) and the environmentalist Green Party (5.7%) were the only other parties to make it into the state parliament.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz's CDU suffered disastrous losses, failing to secure a seat in parliament with only 4.9% of the vote.

The populist Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW), which combines left-leaning economic, conservative migration and pro-Russian foreign policy initiatives, also fell short of entering the state parliament with 4.8%.
The business-focused Free Democratic Party (FDP) failed to regain a seat, securing only 1.0%.
The AfD will therefore hold 32 seats in the new state parliament, while the SPD will hold 29. The Left Party and the Greens will each hold five seats.
The previous SPD-Left Party coalition no longer has a majority, but a three-party alliance with the Greens would have one. All three parties have ruled out forming coalitions with the AfD.
